newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bank/Portugal may cut rates again after CPI-Cisf.
newsitem.headline: Bank/Portugal may cut rates again after CPI-Cisf.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal (BP), which wrongfooted analysts with a preemptive cut in rates last week, could cut again by around 20 basis points after April inflation figures are released, Banco Cisf said.
"The release of the inflation figures in Spain and Portugal, where (year-on-year) rates under two percent are expected, could lead the central banks to a new cuts in rates," it said.
"Despite the cut (last Friday), the Bank of Portugal has room for a further cut of around 20 basis points," it added.
On Friday, the Bank cut its repo rate 30 basis points to 6.0 percent, surprising analysts who had been expecting a move only after the consumer price index (CPI) is released this week.
It also cut 10 basis points off its absorption, or drain rate to 5.7 percent and lowered the emergency lending rate by the same amount to 7.7 percent.
The Bank of Spain's repo stands at 5.50 percent.
